simple.meaning: גְּשׁוּרִי (Gᵉshûwrîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “a Geshurite (also collectively) or inhabitants of Geshur.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גְּשׁוּרִי (H1651) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 3:14, with occurrences in Deuteronomy, Joshua, 1 Samuel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גְּשׁוּרִי (H1651) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גְּשׁוּרִי (H1651) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גְּשׁוּרִי (Gᵉshûwrîy) / H1651 is traced through Deuteronomy 3:14, Joshua 12:5, Joshua 13:2, Joshua 13:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a Geshurite (also collectively) or inhabitants of Geshur
definitions.full: H1651. Geshuri גְּשׁוּרִי adjective, of a people = substantive ׳הַגּ ; 1 people dwelling in Geshûr (above) Deut 3:14 ; Josh 12:5 ; 13:11 , 13 . 2 a tribe of, or near, the Philistines Josh 13:2 read probably הֵגִּוְרִי We and Dr (on 1Sam 27:8 ), Mey ZAW i. 126 n GFM Judg 1:29 n. , also 1Sam 27:8 , but deleted ᵐ5 (not ᵐ5 L ) compare We Dr; read possibly אשׁורי Hom Aufsätze i. (1892), 9 ; 2Sam 2:9 read ׳הגּ for האשׁורי .

occurrences.englishText: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called them, even Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth Jair, to this day.)
and ruled in Mount Hermon, and in Salecah, and in all Bashan, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
“This is the land that still remains: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites;
and Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan to Salecah;
Nevertheless the children of Israel didn’t drive out the Geshurites, nor the Maacathites: but Geshur and Maacath live within Israel to this day.
David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for those were the inhabitants of the land, who were of old, on the way to Shur, even to the land of Egypt.
